data.title: Sigma Solve H1 profit jumps 64% to ₹19.4 cr as other income boosts earnings
data.description:
Sigma Solve Ltd, an information technology and IT-enabled services company, reported a 63.89 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit for the first half of FY27, even as revenue from operations remained virtually unchanged, with a sharp increase in other income contributing to higher overall income.

The Ahmedabad-based company, listed on the NSE and BSE, reported consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹19.40 crore for the six months ended September 30, 2026, compared with ₹11.84 crore in the corresponding period last year, according to a company statement.

Consolidated total income rose 12.71 per cent to ₹56.30 crore from ₹49.95 crore a year earlier. However, revenue from operations inched up just 0.44 per cent to ₹46.45 crore from ₹46.24 crore, indicating that the improvement in overall income was largely supported by non-operating income rather than growth in the company's core business.

Other income more than doubled to ₹9.86 crore from ₹3.71 crore in the year-ago period, accounting for 17.5 per cent of consolidated total income, compared with about 7.4 per cent a year earlier.

The company's consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 29.05 per cent to ₹16.27 crore from ₹12.60 crore. The EBITDA margin, calculated as a percentage of revenue from operations, expanded to 35.02 per cent from 27.26 per cent, an improvement of 7.76 percentage points.

Profit before tax rose 64.26 per cent to ₹25.67 crore from ₹15.63 crore in the corresponding period of FY26.

The PAT margin increased to 41.76 per cent from 25.60 per cent.

While the consolidated numbers point to a substantial improvement in profitability, Sigma Solve's standalone financial performance was comparatively subdued.

Standalone revenue from operations declined to ₹16.29 crore in H1 FY27 from ₹19.21 crore a year earlier. Total income fell to ₹16.99 crore from ₹20.07 crore.

Standalone EBITDA decreased to ₹3.95 crore from ₹4.14 crore, while profit after tax declined to ₹3.01 crore from ₹3.18 crore.

Sigma Solve said it would continue to strengthen its technology capabilities, expand its service portfolio and improve execution to address changing enterprise technology requirements.

The company operates across enterprise software development, cloud solutions, data engineering, business intelligence, analytics, artificial intelligence-driven solutions, digital transformation and automation.

These areas are increasingly central to corporate technology spending as businesses look to modernise legacy systems, automate workflows, improve operational efficiency and deploy data-driven applications.

Commenting on the results, Prakash R. Parikh, Chairman and Managing Director of Sigma Solve, said: "We remain focused on strengthening our technology capabilities, expanding our service portfolio and capitalising on emerging opportunities across Artificial Intelligence, digital transformation and enterprise technology solutions. Our focus continues to be on deepening client relationships, enhancing execution capabilities and delivering technology solutions that address the evolving needs of businesses. We remain committed to building a scalable business platform and creating sustainable long-term value for our stakeholders."

Separately, Sigma Solve said it had recommended a final dividend of ₹0.50 per equity share of Re 1 face value for FY26, representing a 50 per cent dividend on face value. The payout was subsequently approved by shareholders at the company's annual general meeting in September 2026.

The company said it had declared dividends in each of the four consecutive years since its listing in June 2023, highlighting its stated focus on shareholder returns alongside business expansion.

Incorporated in Ahmedabad on April 29, 2010, Sigma Solve provides enterprise technology solutions through its Indian operations and wholly owned US subsidiary, Sigma Solve Inc. Its offerings span software development, cloud computing, data engineering, analytics, AI-led applications and business process automation.

data.title: Stock Futures Jump as AI Trade Set for Rebound
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

U.S. stock futures are poised to open in the green for a shortened trading session Friday, as the artificial-intelligence trade rebounds at the end of a volatile week.

Nasdaq futures trade 2.7% higher, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.8% and 1.15% respectively. Stocks across the AI ecosystem rallied premarket, with Nvidia gaining around 4.5%.

Signs of a rebound follow choppy trade earlier in the week. However, the AI trade isn't out of the woods yet, XTB research director Kathleen Brooks said.

"While technical indicators suggest that a recovery could be on the cards, the fundamental problems surrounding the AI trade remain," Brooks said. "The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered, for example, concerns about the profitability of the AI trade and financing costs."

Gains in the U.S. premarket followed a bullish session in Asia. South Korea's memory chip-dominated Kospi jumped 4.3%, while stock indexes in Shanghai and Hong Kong rose after Chinese authorities reiterated their support for capital markets. European equity indexes rallied at the open, with AI-related stocks leading the charge. The continent's Stoxx 600 index rose 0.95% in early trade.

Improved sentiment in equity markets bled into metals, too. Silver contracts jumped more than 10% to $44.11 a troy ounce, while gold futures added close to 4% to trade around $3,680 an ounce.

Oil prices continued to rise, with benchmark Brent crude contracts gaining 1% to trade around $97.50 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts jumped 2.6% to trade around $85.90 a barrel.

Treasurys weakened amid investors' shift back to risk and hardened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. Ten-year yields rose more than seven basis points to trade above 4.900%, while two-year yields rose toward 4.700%. The Fed enters a blackout period on Saturday ahead of its December meeting, with expectations for a 25 basis point rise priced in at 99%, according to LSEG.

The dollar edged higher against a basket of global currencies but remained below highs hit earlier this week. Bitcoin was helped by broader ebullient market sentiment, rising 1.5% to trade around $61,670.

Spanish voters head to the polls on Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez looks to stay in power. Next week, Nvidia's reinstated Chief Executive Jensen Huang will appear in front of Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday.

data.title: Global equity funds log biggest weekly outflow in 14 months
data.description:
Global equity funds recorded their largest weekly outflow in 14 months in the week to November 25 as growing concerns over returns on investments in the AI build-out and hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve officials dampened appetite for risk assets.

Investors liquidated a net $22.73 billion from global equity funds during the week, marking their largest weekly net sales since September 17, 2025, LSEG Lipper data showed.

Fund investors turned cautious last week as a technology selloff, driven by concerns over returns on AI infrastructure investments, pushed global stock indexes to seven-month lows.

The MSCI All Country World Index EURONEXT:IACWI fell to 1,019.01 last week, its lowest level since April 8. The index has, however, recovered about 3.5% so far this week.

"We estimate that overall revenues for AI models and applications will have to grow at least 750% over the next four years for the industry to earn an adequate return to justify the cumulative spending," said Mark Haefele, chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, in a note on Thursday.

"We maintain a Neutral view on global and US equities, reflecting a balanced risk-reward outlook."

US equity funds recorded net weekly outflows of $30.57 billion, the largest since September 9. Investors also withdrew a net $2.75 billion from Asian funds but added $7.29 billion to European funds.

Among sector funds, technology, healthcare and industrial funds came under pressure, with investors pulling a net $7.57 billion, $3.04 billion and $2.56 billion, respectively.

Global bond funds recorded a third consecutive weekly outflow, totalling a net $3.51 billion.

Investors sold a net $5.85 billion from dollar-denominated medium-term bond funds, $2.73 billion from euro-denominated bond funds and $1.54 billion from high-yield bond funds. However, they bought a net $7.14 billion of government bond funds and $1.17 billion of short-term bond funds.

Money market funds posted a third straight weekly outflow, totalling a net $49.42 billion.

Among commodity funds, gold and other precious metals funds recorded net outflows of $2.14 billion, their largest since March 25. Energy funds also saw outflows of $463 million.

In emerging markets, equity funds attracted a net $971 million for an eighth consecutive week. Bond funds, however, posted a fifth straight weekly outflow of $1.42 billion, based on data covering 29,180 funds.

data.title: Italian ex-police chief drawn into mafia probe defends his record in suicide note
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ex-police chief claims innocence
  • Probe linked to Borsellino case preceded suicide
  • Italian president expected to attend funeral

By Angelo Amante

A former top Italian security official who took his own life last week while under investigation for allegedly obstructing a probe into a 34-year-old mafia assassination defended his record in a suicide note released on Friday.

Gianni De Gennaro was found dead at his country house in Tuscany on November 21, aged 78. Prosecutors had sought his arrest in a new investigation into the killing of anti-mafia judge Paolo Borsellino, who died in a car bomb attack in 1992.

"Within a few minutes, I will no longer be here, and so you can well understand that a man condemned to death cannot lie," De Gennaro said in a letter published in full by the Corriere della Sera newspaper.

"I always obeyed the orders I was given and carried out the duties entrusted to me, even when I would have preferred not to, with commitment and dedication," he wrote, adding that he had served his country "with honesty and loyalty".

Reuters could not independently verify the authenticity of the letter.

De Gennaro's death has sent shockwaves throughout Italy's political establishment.

He was national police chief from 2000 to 2007 after playing an important role in the fight against the Sicilian Cosa Nostra mafia in the 1980s and 1990s. He also led the intelligence services and served as chairman of defence firm Finmeccanica-Leonardo .

FUNERAL ON MONDAY

De Gennaro's funeral is scheduled for Monday in Rome, with guests expected to include President Sergio Mattarella, according to media reports.

Prosecutors in the Sicilian city of Caltanissetta are investigating alleged efforts to derail the inquiry that followed Borsellino's murder.

Police initially identified suspects who were later found innocent, and magistrates are examining allegations that investigators coerced false confessions. The reasons for this are disputed.

Prosecutors suspect De Gennaro may have been involved, an allegation he denied. A judge this month rejected a request to place him under house arrest, saying there was insufficient evidence.

Corriere said his final letter, dated November 20, was recovered alongside a hard drive that police had failed to find during searches of De Gennaro's residences linked to the investigation.

"It does not contain any mysteries or secrets," De Gennaro said about the drive, saying it was a professional archive which he did not want falling into the hands of people he considered unable to properly evaluate its contents.

data.title: Polish poultry exports at risk as bird flu returns after six-month break
data.description:
By Marta Maciag and Canan Sevgili

Poultry exports from Poland, the European Union's largest producer, are likely to be hit by the detection of bird flu outbreaks, and the sector should prepare for further cases, veterinary authorities said on Thursday.

Poland detected an outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly known as bird flu, on a turkey farm last week, the country's first outbreak in commercial poultry in nearly six months.

The World Organisation for Animal Health reported another case in Poland on Thursday, at a mixed-species farm housing ducks, chickens and geese.

Poland is the European Union's largest producer and exporter of poultry meat. It produced around 2.9 million tons of meat in 2024, accounting for 20.5% of the bloc's total output, EU data showed.

Poland's National Poultry Council said bird flu outbreaks could affect exports.

"More than half of domestic production goes to foreign markets. For this reason, an increase in the number of HPAI (bird flu) outbreaks could have significant consequences for the functioning of the entire poultry sector," council president Dariusz Goszczynski said.

The General Veterinary Inspectorate stressed that the scale and scope of any potential restrictions could be regionalised, meaning they would be limited to affected areas or to a wider surrounding zone.

A regional veterinary authority based in the city of Olsztyn in northern Poland said the return of the virus after a six-month break was a significant epidemiological warning and that further outbreaks should be expected, although their scale and geographical spread remained uncertain.

"The possibility of further outbreaks of the disease should certainly be anticipated, although at the current stage it cannot be determined what their scale or range will be," the regulator said.

data.title: Germany's Rheinmetall trims 2030 ambitions after project setbacks
data.description:
German defence company Rheinmetall has cut its targets for 2030 to take into account a "new normal level of conservatism" after several project setbacks this year.

The company now expects sales between €33 billion and €37 billion ($36 billion-$41 billion) in the midterm, according to presentation slides published on Friday for its Capital Markets Day, down from around €45 billion it had previously forecast.

Europe's largest ammunition maker has profited immensely from the continent's renewed armament push since Russia invaded Ukraine in early 2022. However, it has faced problems translating that demand into firm orders.

The company had cut its 2026 forecast for a second time in three months earlier this month, sending shares tumbling. On Friday, shares were up 4.3% shortly after the event started.

Rheinmetall adopted a more conservative tone after the German government's cancellation of the F126 frigate programme, delays to advance payments linked to Germany's Arminius Boxer vehicle programme as well as ammunition approval bottlenecks.

Separately, Rheinmetall on Friday announced that it will supply an additional 66 Lynx armoured vehicles to Romania, with an order value at around €738 million.

($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: FX firm as sentiment improves, Hungary ratings review in focus
data.description:
Central European currencies mostly firmed on Friday, recouping some of their losses from earlier this week, with the Hungarian forint leading gains as investors eyed a sovereign rating review by S&P due to be published later in the day after market close.

The Polish zloty was up 0.35% and trading at 4.466 to the euro, firming back from a fresh three-year low hit in the previous session.

"Volatility in the financial markets may remain limited. In the US, trading is taking place today, though the session is shortened due to the long holiday weekend," Bank Millennium wrote in a note.

"Meanwhile, global stock markets are seeing an improvement in sentiment, driven by the Chinese government’s pledge to support its local equity market ... This is providing a boost to emerging market currencies," they added.

On Friday, Beijing vowed to strengthen the role of the state-backed "national team" in helping to stabilize a market that has struggled this year. The "national team" is markets' nickname for China's state-backed investors.

The Hungarian forint gained 0.45% and was trading at 370.15 per euro, regaining some of its losses from earlier this week.

"The forint is correcting. The Hungarian currency has managed to strengthen, bringing the euro-forint rate back into its previous trend channel. The upper boundary of that channel is at 371.00, while the next key support level is located at 369.50," brokerage Equilor wrote in a note.

In Hungary, investors eyed ratings agency S&P's sovereign ratings review, scheduled to be published after markets close.

"Last Friday, Moody’s improved its outlook from negative to stable, and we expect a similar outcome from S&P today. However, the market has likely already priced in this good news, so it is unlikely to be a market mover," ING wrote in a note.

Elsewhere, the Czech crown added 0.15% to trade at 24.431 to the euro.

Stock markets in the region gained, with Warsaw and Budapest adding 2% each. Prague's blue chip index was 0.6% higher.

data.title: Zambia's central bank maintains policy rate, says stance appropriate
data.description:
Zambia's central bank kept its benchmark lending rate (ZMCBIR=ECI) unchanged at 10.75% in a decision announced on Friday, noting inflation was within its target band and that it was projected to remain there.

  • The Monetary Policy Committee concluded that the current policy stance was appropriate, Governor Denny Kalyalya told a press conference

  • Annual inflation was at 6.4% (ZMCPIY=ECI) year on year in November, up slightly from 6.3% in October and within the Bank of Zambia's 6%-8% target range

  • In September the central bank cut its Monetary Policy Rate by 250 basis points

data.title: Indian central bank trims sale of 2029 bond as rising bets on hefty rate hike lift yields
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

The Indian central bank accepted bids worth about 40% of the size of shorter-tenor three-year bonds in an auction on Friday, managing to keep the cutoff yield below 7% handle, as a chorus for an outsized interest rate hike next week pushed up yields.

Here are some more details:

  • Reserve Bank of India accepted bids worth 36.8 billion rupees ($396.80 million) in the planned 90-billion-rupee auction of the 6.20% 2029 paper

  • The three-year or 6.20% 2029 bond yield was dealt at 6.9960% in the secondary market before the auction cutoffs, and there were no deals after the auction

  • "Investors must have demanded yields above 7%, especially with the central bank meeting just a week away, and the RBI would not be comfortable (with that)," trader with a private bank said

  • RBI had last partially cancelled the auction of this security in September

  • RBI policy decision is due on December 4, with a rising number of economists now calling for a 50-basis-point hike

  • Nomura and Deutsche Bank jumped on the bandwagon on Friday and have recommended front-loaded hikes to fight elevated inflationary pressures

  • RBI sold a seven-year bond at a slightly higher-than-expected yield, while ultra-long 30-year paper was sold at yields that were in line with estimates

($1 = 92.7425 Indian rupees)

data.title: Prices fall on milder temperature forecasts, strong Norwegian supply
data.description:
Key points:
  • Milder temperatures expected on latest weather run
  • Supply from Norway rises
  • Europe's gas stores 67.20% full

Dutch and British gas prices fell on Friday morning as forecasts for milder temperatures curbed demand and supply from Norway rose.

The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was down €3.428 at €84.40 per megawatt hour (MWh) or around $27.10 /mmBtu, by 0918 GMT, ICE data showed.

The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) was down 9.47 pence at 208.30 pence per therm.

“Weather across north-west Europe is set to get warmer on the DA (day-ahead)," said LSEG gas analyst Dzmitry Dauhalevich, with the forecast 3 degrees Celsius higher than previously at 3.5C.

Local distribution zone demand, which includes heating demand, is forecast 623 gigawatt hours/day lower at 4,353 GWh/d for the day-ahead, LSEG data showed.

Norwegian exports to continental Europe, which have been curbed by outages and maintenance this week, were forecast to rise by 35 million cubic metres day to 341 mcm/d, LSEG data showed.

In Britain, strong wind power output also led to lower gas demand.

Peak wind power output was forecast at 19.9 gigawatts on Friday and 19.7 GW for Saturday, Elexon data showed.

Europe, however, remains vulnerable to cold weather shocks with gas stores at low levels.

Germany, Europe’s largest gas consumer, “faces the lowest stock levels in more than a decade heading into winter, and the weather forecasts so far look cold for at least the first week of December,” analysts at Mind Energy said.

Europe’s gas stores are currently 67.20 % full, the latest data from Gas Infrastructure Europe showed.

In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract <> was up €0.91 at €85.06 euro a metric ton.

data.description:

(09:05 GMT) *Rheinmetall Raises 2030 Oper Margin View

(09:06 GMT) *Rheinmetall Backs 2030 Cash Conversion Rate View

(09:18 GMT) *Correct: Rheinmetall Cuts 2030 Oper Margin View
(09:19 GMT) *Correct: Rheinmetall Sees 2030 Oper Margin Of About 20%, Prior Above 20%
(09:28 GMT) Arms Maker Rheinmetall Slashes Midterm Forecasts After Order Setbacks

By Mauro Orru

Rheinmetall lowered its sales and margin projections for the end of the decade, a sign that it doesn't expect to grow as strongly as it previously forecast after the German government canceled a big frigate order and delayed procurement of a lucrative combat-vehicle project.

The German defense group said its 2030 sales should range between 33 billion euros and 37 billion euros, equivalent to between $36.20 billion and $40.58 billion. The company had previously expected 2030 sales of about 50 billion euros.

Meanwhile, its closely watched operating margin should come in at about 20% at the end of the decade compared with a prior forecast of above 20%. Its cash conversion rate is still expected above 50%.

The revisions show that Rheinmetall is moving to recalibrate expectations for the coming years following a number of setbacks in recent months that weighed on its stock and led some analysts to question whether the midterm targets it had tweaked last year were still achievable. Rheinmetall slashed its 2026 guidance twice this year and its shares are down nearly 50% since early January.

data.title: TVS Motor Company Introduces TVS Armado, a New Cargo Tricycle
data.description:
TVS Motor Company, part of TVS VENU, and a reputed global manufacturer of two and three-wheelers, today announced the global launch of TVS Armado – the best-in-class cargo tricycle with 1 ton load capacity. With this launch TVS expands its commercial mobility portfolio with a tricycle designed to address the evolving needs of cargo transportation and first and last-mile logistics.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261126523378/en/

Beyond the product itself, TVS Armado is backed by the assurance associated with the TVS Motor brand. The company's focus on quality, reliability, genuine spare parts availability, trained service personnel and customer support is intended to help commercial users maintain their vehicles and businesses with confidence.

Recognizing the needs of entrepreneurs, fleet owners, delivery businesses - TVS Armado has been developed with a customer-first approach, translating real-world operating requirements into a dependable mobility solution that is designed to keep businesses moving day in, day out.

The TVS Armado is powered by a robust 200 cc oil-cooled engine, delivering 10.6 kW of maximum power at 7,500 rpm and 15.5 Nm of peak torque at 5,000 rpm, paired with a five-speed manual transmission. Designed for demanding commercial mobility solutions, it features a 16-litre fuel tank to support extended operating hours. Its two-metre long cargo bed offers a vast loading area with payload capacity of up to 1 ton, enabling businesses to transport a wide range of goods efficiently. The large cargo bed, along with 230 mm of ground clearance and strong leaf spring suspension is designed to support operations across varied road conditions, including urban, suburban and rural routes. The first in industry oil-cooled engine is designed to offer a practical balance of durability and ease of maintenance, backed with the best-in-category warranty terms which reinforces customer confidence in long-term ownership.

Speaking at the global launch, Peyman Kargar, President, International Business, TVS Motor Company said, “TVS Motor has always believed in providing innovative mobility solutions. With TVS Armado, we become the first globally reputed OEM to enter the tricycle cargo segment, bringing an innovative, best-in-class product to the 1 ton cargo mobility space. First- and last-mile logistics is critical to businesses and communities, and TVS Armado is designed around the real needs of customers and business owners, combining load-carrying capability, world-class reliability and durability with the practicality required for everyday commercial use.

“As we build our commercial mobility portfolio globally, TVS Armado reflects our ambition to create solutions that deliver tangible business value and contribute to the growth of communities. TVS Armado aims to be a reliable business partner for those who work relentlessly to build a better future, in line with TVS Motor’s vision of transforming the quality of life of people across the world by providing mobility solutions that are exciting, responsible, sustainable and safe.”

With TVS Armado, TVS Motor Company builds on its experience in commercial mobility to address the evolving needs of cargo transportation. TVS Armado aims to be a reliable business partner for those who work relentlessly to build a better future across the regions of Africa, Latin America and ASEAN.

For more information, please visit www.tvsmotor.com
